newsitem.title: USA: CME live cattle end mixed, feeders higher.
newsitem.headline: CME live cattle end mixed, feeders higher.

text.p: CME live cattle futures closed mixed with December pressured by spreading, while feeder cattle closed higher supported by strong gains in cash prices, traders said.

Fundamentals continued to support cattle futures, but transferring long December positions to February weighed on December. Traders said the spreading appeared to be associated with the "Goldman Roll". The roll occurs in commodity futures used in the Goldman Sachs Commodity Index and generally begins early in the month preceding the delivery month.
Higher cash beef prices were supportive as were continued ideas $72.00 per cwt will be paid in High Plains feedlot markets this week.
"Before the week is out, $72 will be paid everywhere," said one trader.
"$72 is priced in the market," said Jim Clarkson, analyst with A and A Inc. "They better get it, because if they don't this break (in the futures) will be even greater."

Buying in feeder cattle was fueled by the sharp gain in the CME average feeder cattle index and lower CBOT corn futures. Traders said with corn prices dropping feedlots can profitably hedge feeder cattle against the deferred live cattle futures.
The latest CME feeder cattle price rose 0.82 cent to 63.21. CBOT corn futures closed lower.
Live cattle closed down 0.200 to up 0.025 cent with December the only lower contract at 67.025.
Feeder cattle were up 0.150 to 0.700 cent with November up 0.150 at 65.450. Contract highs were set in the January 1997 and forward feeder cattle contracts.
